quotes.quote: the first month they are not allowed to shape a single loaf
the starter is the whole bakery
the failure happened twelve hours before they touched the dough
the patience of reading back through your own records instead of guessing
Not his shaping, not his scoring, the fact that he noticed the starter.
the slow invisible part of the work, the part that happens before anyone sees anything
half the agenda is status updates that could be a written document
we spent seventy minutes on updates and twenty minutes on the one decision that actually mattered
The thing that needs the whole room gets the least time.
the Monday meeting is only for decisions and disagreements. If there is no decision on the agenda, we cancel the meeting.
each update is three lines, what changed, what is blocked, what decision you need
the meeting facilitator should change every week
I keep stalling because every draft feels too small
I have a feeling, not an argument.
Nobody wrote back to the big abstract ones. So why do I keep starting with the abstract?
But the small specific thing is the only way a reader gets in.
Write the toolbox, not the thesis.
The small invisible daily thing, the starter, the notebook, the toolbox. Maybe that is the actual essay. I don't know yet.
Is it one piece or three pieces? I genuinely can't tell.
